extra.message: Broken object-level authorization (IDOR): the account_id query parameter is read directly from the request and used as the lookup key into folio_cards, then returned to the caller. Any caller passing the internal gate can retrieve another account's folio data simply by changing account_id; there is no ownership or tenant check tying the record to the requesting identity.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Path traversal (arbitrary file read): packet_ref comes from request.GET and is joined directly onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR with the / operator before read_text(). A value such as ../../../../etc/passwd escapes the export directory and the file contents are returned to the client in the HTTP response.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF): the url query parameter is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen() without any allowlist or scheme/host validation. An attacker can make the server issue requests to internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, http://localhost:5432) and the response body preview is returned to the caller.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: Parameter tampering / mass assignment: the amount and state fields are taken from the attacker-controlled JSON body (or query string) and applied directly to the ledger record. cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: Open redirect: the lane parameter is read from GET/POST and passed to Django's redirect() without validating that it is a local path. An attacker can craft /ops/after/acct-lane-161/?lane=https://evil.example to redirect victims to an arbitrary external site for phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Mass assignment / privilege escalation: the request JSON payload is merged wholesale into the workset dictionary via workset.update(payload), overwriting sensitive fields such as role, approved and balance. cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: Path traversal (arbitrary file write) plus cleartext storage of sensitive data: ref comes from request.GET and is interpolated into the target path BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json" before write_text(). A value like ../../some/path escapes the export directory and allows writing attacker-controlled JSON anywhere the process can write. extra.message: Use of a broken cryptographic hash: hashlib.md5() is used to hash the user-supplied phrase. MD5 is collision-prone and unsuitable for security purposes (password storage, integrity, signatures). An attacker-controlled input can be crafted to produce collisions.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
